articles.title: 2026 Kindle Paperwhite review: Page-turn buttons are back, for a price
articles.summary: Supply pressures, shortages, and inflation have pushed tech prices relentlessly upward over the last half-decade, and even basic gadgets haven't been immune. That's why you can spend $385 on a Raspberry Pi, or why the cheapest Amazon Kindle in 2026 costs more than the midrange one from a few years…
body: The 2024 Kindles all came with small price increases, but the 2026 models make them look like stellar deals. The $160 Kindle Paperwhite from two years ago wipes the floor with this year’s $150 Kindle in just about every conceivable way, from screen size to front light quality to waterproofing—something to consider if you’re choosing between a used or refurbished Paperwhite and one of these new models.

The flagship of the now five-model-large monochrome Kindle family is the $250 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition, which takes the core specs of the new $200 Paperwhite and puts it in a sturdy iPad-esque aluminum case instead of the typical plastic.

It’s an exceptionally nice reader, and if you’re down with paying even more for it, longtime page-turn button holdouts can recover their precious buttons while still getting the benefits of new, fast Kindle hardware. With the exception of one regression—wireless charging, a feature of the 2024 Signature Edition that has been removed here—it’s the fastest and nicest Kindle you can get. It’s mostly the value, or lack thereof, that leaves a bad taste in one’s mouth.

articles.title: Kodak’s adorable Charmera keychain camera is on sale for just $30
articles.summary: We wouldn’t normally recommend a bad camera, but we’ll make an exception for the Kodak Charmera. As my colleague Andrew Liszewski pointed out in his review, the tiny retro keychain camera takes pretty lackluster photos, yet it’s charming enough that he kept using it anyway.
body: The tiny keychain camera is a ton of fun to use, even if its photos are laughably bad.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The Charmera is small enough to carry on your keys and comes in a blind box, so you won’t know which of the six retro designs or the rarer transparent version you’re getting until you open it. It’s a simple point-and-shoot with a tiny LCD screen, and its 1,440x1,080-pixel photos often look fuzzy and washed out. Some of the built-in effects can make the results more interesting, though. Liszewski had some fun with the black-and-white mode and found that the red, blue, yellow, and gray pixel filters could produce bolder two-tone images. Video and audio quality are poor, too, and you can’t adjust much to improve them. Still, for a $30 keychain, it offers a surprising amount to play with.

The Charmera isn’t something you’d want to rely on for an important occasion, but it can be fun to experiment with. Liszewski found that even though most pictures weren’t worth keeping, he’d occasionally get one interesting enough to share. That makes it a fun stocking stuffer for someone who loves cute, unusual gadgets.

articles.title: Pensions and benefits services still down after 'cyber incident'
articles.summary: The UK's former chief technology officer says the Department for Work and Pensions may have been hit by hackers, but the government has not confirmed that.
body: Online benefits and pensions services were still down on Saturday morning following a "cyber incident" which forced the government to take them offline.
The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has not specified what triggered it to shut down access late on Thursday but has not ruled out that it was hit by hackers.

The government has assured benefits recipients and pensioners that usual payments will continue to be made after some claimants reported delays. It is understood the department believes delays were not linked to the cyber incident.
The UK's former chief technology officer David Knott told BBC Newsnight his "strong suspicion" was that the department had been targeted by hackers.

articles.title: Swift Saw the Secrets of Space Before Falling to Earth
articles.summary: Designed for a two-year mission, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory saw thousands of gamma-ray bursts and stars being torn apart by black holes over 22 years before burning up in Earth’s atmosphere.
body: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has concluded its scientific mission, which spanned just under 22 years. As its orbital altitude fell below 275 kilometers (171 miles), it could no longer continue stable astronomical observations, and it reentered the atmosphere on November 4 over North Sumatra, Indonesia.

Swift had been launched on November 20, 2004, as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer, and it began operations the following month. In addition to a gamma-ray-burst alert telescope, it was equipped with ultraviolet and visible-light telescopes as well as an x-ray telescope, and was designed as a multi-wavelength observation satellite capable of rapidly pinpointing the locations of gamma-ray bursts—the most powerful explosions in the universe. In 2018, following the death of its first principal investigator, Neil Gehrels, NASA renamed the mission in his honor.
points: Designed for a two-year mission, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory saw thousands of gamma-ray bursts and stars being torn apart by black holes over 22 years before burning up in Earth’s atmosphere.

articles.title: Dark Matter Might Have Its Own Periodic Table of Invisible Particles
articles.summary: Although it remains within the realm of theoretical physics, a new study hints at a parallel chemistry that would force us to rethink how we organize the fundamental components of the universe.
body: Dark matter accounts for approximately 85 percent of all matter in the universe, though that’s about all we really know about the mysterious substance. Scientists believe it because of the gravitational effects it has on galaxies and other cosmic structures, but since it doesn’t otherwise interact with ordinary matter, it’s been a challenge for scientists to determine what it’s really made of.

For decades, scientists have been trying to determine whether dark matter consists of a single type of particle or if it’s made up of several particles that could have different properties and thus different interactions with the surrounding world. Earlier this year, scientists found the most convincing evidence of a dark matter particle yet, and if the second scenario is true, it’s possible we could find more.

This second possibility also raises an intriguing question: If there are a variety of “dark particles,” could they interact and combine with one another—just as the particles we know do —to form their own dark atoms and molecules? If that were the case, the dark universe could be much more complex than researchers had initially imagined.
points: Although it remains within the realm of theoretical physics, a new study hints at a parallel chemistry that would force us to rethink how we organize the fundamental components of the universe.

articles.title: Why updating your iPhone can improve your CarPlay experience
articles.summary: Wondering how to update CarPlay? The answer isn't on your car's screen. Here's where to look and what new features you could be missing out on.
body: Skipping iPhone updates can cost you new CarPlay features. Here's what you could be missing.

CarPlay is a great way to get all of your music, contacts and addresses on your car's infotainment system. But CarPlay isn't an app installed on your car. It runs straight from your iPhone, so the car usually doesn't have an "update CarPlay" option of its own. To update CarPlay, you need to update iOS.

CarPlay keeps working even if you don't update your phone, but you'll miss out on the new features, bug fixes and compatibility improvements. iOS 27, released September 14, added an audio mini-player, plus route sharing and video apps on supported cars. Apple says it also improves wireless CarPlay reliability and GPS accuracy. Here's how updating your iPhone can improve your CarPlay experience.

To update your iPhone, go to Settings > General > Software Update and check your iOS version. If a newer one is available, it will be waiting for you there. The latest version at the time of writing is iOS 27.2.1 (November 9). Phones still on iOS 26 will see a small iOS 26 update and the larger iOS 27 upgrade as separate options.

articles.title: How you can give your old DJI drone new purpose
articles.summary: An older DJI drone can still fly steady and shoot great video. Find out how to give yours a second act that goes well beyond the junk drawer.
body: You don’t need to risk a brand new DJI drone for practice, specific tasks and aerial pics.

An old DJI drone is still a nice, working drone, and unless it's a wrecked heap of scrap, it has plenty of life ahead of it. Besides, it's a much better teacher than a new DJI Matrice 5T, because crashing it is a lot less scary than crashing the $8,000 beast that just emptied your bank account. As long as it still gets updates, swap out the worn props, give the batteries a once-over and let your archaic DJI drone be a kamikaze risk-taker or a solid spare.

Now that it's been replaced, its best job is practice, especially for new maneuvers or teaching someone else how to fly one. When you want to work on tight turns or low approaches, risk the geriatric version and spare your best drone. Leave the new one in the box for risky flights through heavy tree canopies or over water.

The old one also makes for a good spare in case the newbie runs out of juice or face-plants into a brick wall. Depending on your model, add-ons like the Sky Rigger make it a good fit for dropping bait when fishing.

Earlier this month, Apple introduced subscription retention messages, which give developers a way to convince you to stay, whether with a message or even a special discount.
